commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify find examples and name input
commitResults.messageBody:
The find examples use contacts from the old sample data, but
TutorRoster now starts with an empty list, so the examples return no
matches on a fresh launch. Testers may also type find n/Alex, as in
delete n/NAME, and get no results.

Let's state which contacts the examples assume, and explain that the
name is typed without n/.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify list filter wording and card test
commitResults.messageBody:
The list section says former students are hidden without saying this
is only the default, and says students without a level or subject are
not shown, which reads as if a student missing either field is hidden
by any filter. The manual test for ordering still describes cards as
NAME [ROLE], although cards now show role badges.

Let's state that hiding former students is the default, explain which
filter skips a student without a level or subject, and describe the
current card in the manual test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove fixed-width column from list card
commitResults.messageBody:
List cards keep the 150-pixel grid column from AddressBook-Level3.
Newer JavaFX versions, such as the one bundled with the macOS JDK,
size the card as if it were that wide, so wrapped detail lines leave
blank space below them.

Let's place the card details directly in the card, so their height
depends only on the list's width.
Remove AB3 leftovers from About Us

commitResults.messageTitle: Give view the same index errors as archive
commitResults.messageBody:
view reports a missing index, or more than one index, with the
generic "must be a positive integer" message, while archive and
unarchive say what is wrong and show the command format.

Let's parse the view index with ParserUtil#parseSingleIndex, as
archive does, and document both messages in the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tip on index changes after re-sorting
commitResults.messageBody:
The contact list is always sorted by name, so adding or renaming a
contact can move contacts to different indexes. A user who runs edit 2
twice in a row may change a different contact the second time, and the
user guide does not warn about this.

Let's add a tip under Contact order to check the index again after
the list re-sorts.
Make UG name slash rules consistent for add and edit

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept list prefixes in any letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
add accepts prefixes in any letter case, such as R/student, but list
rejects them as an invalid list command, so a user who types
LIST R/student after an add gets an error.

Let's change the list prefixes to lowercase with ArgumentTokenScanner
before tokenizing, as add does, and update both guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify index tip and duplicate detection limits in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding or editing a contact also resets any search or filter, so
indexes can change without a rename. Same-name contacts are compared
only when a phone or email matches, or both lack the same field, so
a phone-only and an email-only contact are not flagged either.
